purpose: Record historical glass-eel recruitment evidence at the Cagayan River mouth without treating estuarine recruits as a complete freshwater checklist, current presence, or abundance estimate.

source.title: Seasonal Changes in Species Composition of Glass Eels of the Genus Anguilla (Teleostei: Anguillidae) Recruiting to the Cagayan River, Luzon Island, the Philippines
source.citation: Aoyama, J., Yoshinaga, T., Shinoda, A., Shirotori, F., Yambot, A. V., & Han, Y.-S. (2015). Seasonal Changes in Species Composition of Glass Eels of the Genus Anguilla (Teleostei: Anguillidae) Recruiting to the Cagayan River, Luzon Island, the Philippines. Pacific Science, 69(2), 263–270. https://doi.org/10.2984/69.2.8
source.license: No article-specific Creative Commons or reuse terms were identified in the reviewed early-view PDF or article information. Freely accessible PDF is not treated as a reuse grant.

study.waterbody: Cagayan River mouth and estuary, northern Luzon.
samplingPeriods: November 2011–December 2012 (abstract and methods); the discussion elsewhere gives November 2011–November 2012. Preserve this date discrepancy.
study.samplingMethod: Monthly glass-eel samples from one commercial fisher's set nets at the river mouth; morphology and genetic methods were used for identification.
study.molecularSampling: The paper reports genetic identification of long-finned samples and a 1,209-individual molecular subsample in Period II; genetic data were available from the corresponding author upon request, not as a linked public record table in this review.

evidenceLimits: The authors explicitly state their sampled numbers do not represent absolute recruitment abundance; monthly sample volume varied with catch and price.
The study measures glass-eel recruitment at the estuary, not resident adults or distribution across the Cagayan basin, its tributaries, or all inland waterbodies.
The figure marks a collection area near the river mouth but no coordinate series or reusable survey boundary was reviewed; do not digitize it as species geometry.
The two sampling periods are historical. They do not establish current presence, current abundance, fishing permission, catchability, or a legal season.
The article's later discussion has a one-month difference in the end of Period II relative to its abstract and methods.
No article-specific reuse license was identified; do not reproduce its tables, figures, or extended text in app data without rights review or permission.

relationshipToOtherSources.cascoEtAl2025: A separate study at a Toran landing site sampled a 2023 fyke-net catch with glass-eel target species and many bycatch taxa. Gear, period, and sampled catch differ; combine no counts or localities.
relationshipToOtherSources.hilarioEtAl2022: The official UPLB abstract reports 63 eels from Cagayan River and species identification by morphology/molecular methods, but collection dates, sites, and sample-level accessions remain unreviewed in the current registry entry. Keep this as a separate pending evidence lead.

nextAction: Seek independently licensed Region II river, lake, reservoir, and wetland fish surveys with species-to-station dates, vouchers or accessions. Separately pursue full text and sample details for the official UPLB 2022 Cagayan eel study; preserve its station/date gap until verified.
